title: Connection fragmentation causing intermittent 5xx cascades; implement fastpath fallback & retry scheduler
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Several customers reported sustained bursts of 5xx errors and timeouts during peak traffic windows. Preliminary traces show a correlation between connection fragmentation at the frontdoor layer (short keepalive/resets across CDN/proxy hops) and a spike in backend inference failures when requests are retried aggressively by clients. The observed pattern: fragmented request body or mid-stream connection reset -> backend runtime sees partial stream/aborted KV cache access -> 5xx or internal timeout -> client retries -> rapid replays amplify pressure and push warm workers into compaction/GC, producing additional 5xxs.
impact: Multiple mid-market customers experienced degraded availability during three incidents in Feb 2025 (60–120 minute windows). Customer-visible latency increased 2–4x and error rates spiked to 8–15% for affected routes. Business impact: high — two customers submitted escalations and requested dedicated mitigation.
hypothesis_and_findings: Root hypothesis: frontdoor connection fragmentation combined with client retry behavior creates a microburst that exhausts warm worker resources and triggers internal runtime failure modes (KV cache compaction and OOM-like stalls). Supporting evidence: (1) request traces show connection reset at frontdoor followed by immediate retry within <500ms, (2) worker telemetry reports sudden KV compaction cycles aligned with spikes, (3) edge proxy logs indicate mismatched TCP keepalive and TLS session renegotiation events for connections traversing an intermediary CDN edge.
proposed_work: 1) Implement a short-term fastpath fallback: when a customer is escalated, route their requests preferentially to a pool of warm workers with aggressive prefix caching and disabled heavy compaction. 2) Build a retry scheduler at the edge that enforces a backoff-cohort header: SDKs and proxies will be asked to honor this header to spread retries over 1–3s windows rather than immediate replays. 3) Introduce a per-connection active-request cap and connection-healing probe (reset+warmup) to avoid reusing fragmented connections for new in-flight requests. 4) Instrument idempotency headers and add traceable request fingerprinting to detect replay storms and automatically trigger a temporary grace-fastpath. 5) Canary rollout: enable for 5 internal customers, monitor error rate and worker compaction metrics for 48 hours before expanding. 6) Update SDK docs and issue a customer-facing mitigation note with recommended SDK version pin that respects backoff-cohort.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fastpath routing can be toggled per-customer via console and defaults to off.
- Edge retry scheduler returns 'retry-cohort' header and reduces immediate retry attempts by 90% in lab replay tests.
- Idempotency/fingerprint instrumentation shows correct deduplication for replayed requests in synthetic tests.
- Canary for 5 customers shows latency and error rate improvement within 48 hours; no regression in unrelated workloads.
- Runbook updated and customer comms draft approved by Support and Product.
